endorsements.quote: Rollback should not be improvised only after a major incident. It should be pre-specified through thresholds, authority lines and communication procedures.

Active monitoring is a heightened state for tools whose use is allowed but whose risk profile requires intensified surveillance. Triggers may include a new site, a new population, a changed electronic health record workflow, borderline subgroup performance, early drift signals or uncertainty about downstream behaviour.
Pre-specified rollback triggers, authority to suspend, communication plan and fallback workflow.
Minimum audit record: output, model version, user, patient or service context, regime conditions, decision state, action taken and review trail.
Some low-risk administrative tools may need only light release controls, while high-risk diagnostic or treatment-support tools require formal governance.

Purchasers should require vendors and implementing organisations to provide an admissibility dossier before routine deployment: intended-use boundaries, model and data provenance, local data-fit checks, subgroup and equity-risk review, workflow-load assessment, monitoring metrics, incident-reporting channels, version-control procedures and pre-specified rollback thresholds.

Version control and change management Can the organisation identify which model, threshold, dataset mapping or workflow version was active? Version log, change-control procedure, validation requirement for updates and deployment history.

Incident reporting and learning Can safety events, near-misses and unexpected consequences be captured and acted upon? Incident-reporting channel, taxonomy, root-cause review, feedback to users and governance committee review.

Human override and contestability Can clinicians question, override or escalate disagreement with the AI output? Override mechanism, documentation field, human-review pathway and protection against automation bias.

Data fitness Are current inputs valid, timely, complete, correctly mapped and within intended provenance? Data-quality checks, missingness thresholds, input-schema validation, provenance record and local data-readiness sign-off.
If the tool is newly introduced in a ward with unfamiliar staff or uncertain subgroup performance, it may be restricted to mandatory clinician review rather than automatic escalation.

unlisted_practices: Evaluate each AI output for admissibility against data fitness, population fit, actionability, workflow capacity, equity, authority, monitoring and reversibility before releasing it into clinical action.
Classify AI outputs into release, restricted release, active monitoring, rollback or HOLD states.

Withhold (HOLD) AI outputs from clinical action when evidence, feasibility, authorisation, equity safeguards, monitoring or auditability are insufficient, and legitimise non-release as a safety function.
Do not treat monitoring capability as optional; make the ability to monitor a condition of eligibility for routine release.
Treat AI governance as a continuing release-control process rather than a one-off approval event.
Evaluate release governance empirically through simulation, shadow-mode evaluation, implementation pilots and post-deployment audit of rollback or HOLD triggers.

screen.reason: This is a perspective paper proposing a deterministic systems intelligence framework for clinical AI governance and release risk management.
